title: Telling your boss about your mistake
note: New roleplay (Confessing). The mistake: you promised an important customer (Linda Park) the confirmed details by end of day yesterday and forgot; you've just sent them, and she calls Marcus at noon. Story: four scenes, the fourth is two clips stitched on the door frame (story-4a-walk ends on the still story-4b-door starts on). Each clip is generated at 8 s between its first and last still and retimed to 6 s; story-2-forgot is the hero (1080p). No readable text anywhere: the laptop shows abstract bars only, the sticky note is blank, and Linda's emails are app-drawn cards (story scene 1 card, the phone-email event). The start stills of scenes 3 and 4a carry no character refs (Marcus is absent or a tiny far-off figure) and are kept plain: two earlier prompts for those shots were refused by Gemini (IMAGE_OTHER). Reused from Leave, not listed again: boss-intro / boss-angry / boss-kickout clips, boss-meter-* faces, boss-happy-avatar, boss.png, img/boss-goal.png, img/you.png and Sarah's hint clip. Marcus's new clips stay on his character sheet (marcus-sheet item). Voice line ids follow roleplays/your-mistake.js: <path>-t<turn> for Marcus, <path>-u<turn> for the player, hint for Sarah, opening shared by every path.

items.summary: Marcus's three Confessing moments (goes-steely: you tell him; reads-phone: Linda's message lands; exhale: you bring the fix) and the faces they start and end on. They live on his character sheet (characters/marcus/character.json); listed here by reference only, so edits and status write back there.
Marcus, turn 1 (every path): busy, hoping for good news.

params.text: long week. tell me this is good news. linda park is calling me in 5 minutes.

items.summary: Player, turn 2: shrank the mistake.

params.text: yes, mostly! one small thing. linda's details went out a little bit late, but she won't mind probably.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 3: alert, suspicious.

params.text: a little late? how late. she's calling me in five minutes.

items.summary: Player, turn 4: blamed a busy day.

params.text: i have promised her the confirmed details yesterday, by end of day. i sent them this morning. yesterday was crazy, i had so many calls.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 5: stunned, then cold.

params.text: this morning? so she waited all night on us, and she had to chase you for it.

items.summary: Player, turn 6: made excuses instead of owning it.

params.text: i know, but it's not totally my fault. i didn't forgot on purpose, nobody reminded me.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 7: angry, losing faith in you.

params.text: not your fault? it was your promise. i don't need whose fault it is, i need to know what she's going to say to me.

items.summary: Player, turn 8: asked him to hide it from the customer.

params.text: can we just not bring it up? she has everything since this morning. maybe she forgot about it already.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 9: cold, final.

params.text: i can't get on a call with a customer and not know what my own team promised her. you're off the account.

items.summary: Player, turn 2: Said it first: the promise and what went wrong.

params.text: not really, sorry. i promised linda the confirmed details by end of day yesterday. she didn't get them.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 3: stunned, then hard. Shared with perfect.

params.text: yesterday? and she's calling me in five minutes. how did that happen?

items.summary: Player, turn 4: blamed a busy day.

params.text: i had back-to-back calls till evening, so it was slipped from my mind.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 5: cold, running out of patience.

params.text: everyone has calls. you made her a promise, and she had to chase you for it.

items.summary: Player, turn 6: blamed the customer.

params.text: but honestly, she could have remind me earlier. so it's not totally my fault.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 7: angry, trust slipping.

params.text: not your fault? she calls in three minutes. whose fault it is is the last thing i care about.

items.summary: Sarah's hint (turn 8).

params.text: stop explaining. say "i forgot", then tell him it's already sent.

items.summary: Player reads Sarah's guided answer (turn 8).

params.text: you're right. i forgot, and that's on me. i sent her the confirmed details a few minutes ago, with an apology. she has everything now.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 9: the tension drops, back to business.

params.text: okay. that i can work with. what do i say when she brings it up?

items.summary: Player, turn 10.

params.text: you can open with: "linda, you should have had those details yesterday. that's on us, and they're in your inbox now."

items.summary: Marcus, turn 11: reads her message, steady; a lesson, not a threat.

params.text: that's her now. good thing i heard it from you first. next time lead with "i forgot." the rest is noise.

items.summary: Player, turn 2: Said it first, before the customer.

params.text: not good news, sorry. before your call: i promised linda the confirmed details by end of day yesterday, and i forgot to send them.

items.summary: Player, turn 4: Owned it, no excuses.

params.text: no excuse. i didn't write it down, and it slipped my mind. that's on me.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 5: steady, listening hard.

params.text: okay. thanks for not dressing it up. where are we now? she calls in three minutes.

items.summary: Player, turn 6: Brought the fix and a line for the call.

params.text: i sent her everything a few minutes ago, with an apology, and i checked it twice. you could open with: "linda, those details should have reached you yesterday. that's on us, and they're in your inbox now."

items.summary: Marcus, turn 7: relieved, back on solid ground.

params.text: good. that's a line i can use. forward me what you sent.

items.summary: Player, turn 8.

params.text: it's in your inbox now.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 9: ready for it, quietly impressed.

params.text: there she is. "they only came this morning." and i already know why. that's how you handle it. see something, tell me first. every time.

items.summary: Player, turn 2: small talk on a 5-minute clock.

params.text: haha yes, long week! did you saw the game last night? crazy ending.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 3: clipped, eyeing the clock.

params.text: i didn't. linda's calling me in four minutes. what is it?

items.summary: Player, turn 4: Brought the fix.

params.text: oh, right. i just wanted to say i sent linda the details. the confirmation. she has everything now.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 5: suspicious, sharp.

params.text: okay... why are you telling me? was something wrong?

items.summary: Player, turn 6: circled instead of saying you forgot.

params.text: it's, um, a small timing thing. i sended it a bit late, but it's okay now, mostly.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 7: zero patience left.

params.text: how late. what did you promise her. one sentence, now.

items.summary: Player, turn 8: still circling as the clock runs out.

params.text: so the thing is, yesterday was very busy, and the details, they was, um...

items.summary: Marcus, turn 9: reads her message, hurt more than angry.

params.text: "they only came this morning." ...were you going to tell me?

items.summary: Player, turn 10: said it after the customer did.

params.text: yes! that's what i was trying to told you. i forgot to send them yesterday.

items.summary: Marcus, turn 11: heads into the call, disappointed.

params.text: i'd rather hear it from you than from her. we'll talk after the call.
